questions.question: In a chief election, a candidate got 60% of the total valid votes. 5% of the total votes were declared invalid. If the total number of votes is 20,800, then the number of valid votes polled in favour of the candidate is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In a chief election, a candidate got 60% of the total valid votes. 

5% of the total votes were declared invalid. 

The total number of votes is 20,800

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

5% of total votes are invalid then 95% of total votes are valid then,

95% of total votes = 95% of 20800 = 0.95 × 20800 = 19760 votes

60% of valid votes earned by the candidate then,

⇒ 60% of 19760

⇒ 60% × 19760

⇒ 0.60 × 19760 = 11856 votes 

**∴ The number of valid votes polled in favour of the candidate is 11856.**

⇒ 57 units = (20800 times 57)/(100) = 11856 votes.

questions.question: A dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price but uses a false weight and thus earns 25% profit. For weighing a kilogram, he uses a false weight of ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Gain percentage = 25%

**Concept used:**

Profit% = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

Let us assume the dealer purchases 1000 gm at Rs. 1000

Let the dealer purchase N gm at Rs. 1000

According to the question,

25 = (1000 - N)/N] × 100

⇒ 25/100 = (1000 - N)/N

⇒ 1/4 = (1000 - N)/N

⇒ N = 4(1000 - N)

⇒ N = 4000 - 4N

⇒ 5N = 4000

⇒ N = 4000/5 = 800 gm

**∴ He uses the weight of 800 gm.**

questions.question: The ratio of the present age of a father to that of his son is 5 ∶ 2. After 5 years their ages will be in the ratio of 7 ∶ 3. The present age of the father is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of present age of father and son = 5 : 2

Ratio of their age after 5 years = 7 : 3

**Calculation:**

Let the present age of father and son be 5x and 2x respectively

Age of father 5 years later = 5x + 5

Age of son 5 years later = 2x + 5

Now, according to question

(5x + 5)/(2x + 5) = 7 : 3

⇒ 3(5x + 5) = 7(2x + 5)

⇒ 15x + 15 = 14x + 35

⇒ 15x + 14x = 35 - 15

⇒ x = 20

Age of father after 5 years = 5x = (5 × 20) = 100 years

**∴ The present age of the father is 100 years.**

questions.question: A can do three-seventh of a work in 15 days and B can do two-fifth of the same work in 14 days. If A and B work together, then how long (in days) will they take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do three-seventh of a work in 15 days 

B can do two-fifth of the same work in 14 days

**Calculations:**

Let the total work be 'x',

Amount of work done by A in one day = (3x/7) × 1/15 = x/35 units

Amount of work done by B in one day = (2x/5) × 1/14 = x/35 units

Amount of work done by A and B both = x/35 + x/35 = 2x/35

Since, x is a total work then,

Time taken to do total work done by A and B both = 2/35 = 35/2 or 17(1)/(2)

**∴ A and B work together they will take 17(1)/(2) to complete the work.**

questions.question: The salary of a typist was first raised by in the first year 20% and then the same was reduced by 15% in the second year. If the typist's present salary is Rs. 1,224, then what was his/her salary two years ago?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

The salary of a typist was first raised by 20% 

The same was reduced by 15%. 

The typist presently draws Rs. 1,224

**Calculation:**

Let the original salary be 'x'

After 20% of increment of salary of typist = x + 20% of x

⇒ x(1+20% )

⇒ x(1 + 20/100)

⇒ x(100 + 20)/100

⇒ 120x/100 = 1.2x

After decremnt of 15% salalry of typist = 1.2x - 15% of 1.2x

⇒ 1.2x(1 - 15% )

⇒ 1.2x(1 - 15/100)

⇒ 1.2x(100 - 15)/100

⇒ 1.2x(85/100)

⇒ 1.2x(0.85) = 1.02x

Salary of typist after increment and decrement = 1.02x

⇒ 1.02 = 1224

⇒ x = 1224/1.02 = 1200

**∴ The salary of typist initially is Rs. 1200.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** Let the salary of the typist = S

Also, reduction in salary = 15% = 3/20 i.e., 3 units decrease out of 20 units = 17/20 units.

⇒ S times(6)/(5)times (17)/(20) = Rs. 1224

⇒ S = (1224 times 5 times 20)/(6×17) = Rs. 1200

questions.question: To go a distance of 144 km upstream, a rower takes 12 hours while it takes her only 9 hours to row the same distance downstream. The speed of the stream is ______.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

To go a distance of 144 km upstream, a rower takes 12 hours 

It takes her only 9 hours to row the same distance downstream

**Concept used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculations:**

Let x be the rower's speed and y be the current speed of water.

Speed while going upstream = (x - y)

144/(x - y) = 12

⇒ x - y = 12 ............(1)

Now speed while going downstream = (x + y)

144/(x + y) = 9

⇒ x + y = 16 ............(2)

Subtracting equation 1 from 2, we get

(x + y) - (x - y) = 16 - 12

⇒ 2y = 4

⇒ y = 4/2 = 2 km/h

**∴ The speed of the stream is 2 km/h.**

questions.question: A tradesman marks his goods at 15% above the cost price and allows purchasers a discount of 10% for cash. What profit percentage does he make?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A tradesman marks his goods at 15% above the cost price 

Allows purchasers a discount of 10% for cash

**Concept used:**

MP = CP(1 + P%)

P% = (SP - CP)/CP × 100

**Calculations:**

Let the CP of goods be 'x'

MP = CP(1 + 15%)

⇒ MP = x(1 + 0.15)

⇒ MP = 1.15x

Now SP of goods

SP = MP(1 - 10%)

⇒ SP = 1.15x(1 - 0.10)

⇒ SP = 1.15x(0.90) = 1.035x

Now Profit%,

P% = [(1.035x - x)/x] × 100

⇒ P% = (0.035x/x) × 100

⇒ P% = 0.035 × 100 = 3.5%

**∴ Profit percentage he makes 3.5%.**

questions.question: A train runs at a speed of 90 km/h in the first 10 min, 60 km/h in the next 20 min, and 40 km/h in the last 5 minutes. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed can be calculated directly by taking the weighted average of speeds using their respective time ratios.

Time ratio (t₁ : t₂ : t₃) = 10 : 20 : 5 ⇒ 2 : 4 : 1

Average Speed = (v₁t₁ + v₂t₂ + v₃t₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃)

⇒ Average Speed = (90 × 2 + 60 × 4 + 40 × 1) ÷ (2 + 4 + 1)

⇒ Average Speed = (180 + 240 + 40) ÷ 7 = 460 ÷ 7 = 65 ⁵/₇ km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 65 ⁵/₇ km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Speed 1 = 90 km/h, Time 1 = 10 min = 10/60 hr = 1/6 hr

⇒ Speed 2 = 60 km/h, Time 2 = 20 min = 20/60 hr = 1/3 hr

⇒ Speed 3 = 40 km/h, Time 3 = 5 min = 5/60 hr = 1/12 hr

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4294157b2fe39e7e1224781bf30c3afe41450aab6ae67c595d7a4e539194f684.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance D₁ = 90 × (1/6) = 15 km

⇒ Distance D₂ = 60 × (1/3) = 20 km

⇒ Distance D₃ = 40 × (1/12) = 10/3 km

⇒ Total Distance = 15 + 20 + 10/3 = 35 + 10/3 = (105 + 10) / 3 = 115/3 km

⇒ Total Time = 1/6 + 1/3 + 1/12 = (2 + 4 + 1) / 12 = 7/12 hr

⇒ Average Speed = (115/3) ÷ (7/12) = (115/3) × (12/7)

⇒ Average Speed = (115 × 4) ÷ 7 = 460 ÷ 7 = 65 ⁵/₇ km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 65 ⁵/₇ km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed can be directly calculated using the formula 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

For three equal distances covered at individual speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is given by 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed Concept

If two bodies move in opposite directions, their effective relative speed is (V₁ + V₂). If they move in the same direction, it is (V₁ − V₂).
